comparison: Both support the selective crowding-induced invasiveness in MCF10DCIS.com cells (C2, C18-C20). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative invasion assay data with controls and reversibility (C71-C72), while peer reviewers highlight the selectivity for highly malignant invasive cell lines and absence in MDA-MB-231. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with strong agreement.

Both support cell volume and stiffness measurements (C21-C24). OpenEval notes validated techniques and correlation analysis (C62-C63), while peer reviewers confirm pre-malignant cells show more pronounced volume reduction. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with full agreement on the measurements.

Perfect alignment on hyperosmotic stress mimicking crowding effects (C25, C75-C76). OpenEval emphasizes dose-response data and viability controls establishing mechanistic causality, while peer reviewers note the use of multiple strategies including hyperosmotic stress showing good correlation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement on mass spectrometry data showing ion channel trafficking to plasma membrane (C3, C26-C29). OpenEval highlights dramatic increases and unchanged total expression via western blot, while peer reviewers confirm TRPV4 relocation both in vitro and in vivo. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support TRPV4 relocation via immunofluorescence (C30-C33, C83-C85). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of cell-type specificity and reversibility (C86-C89), while peer reviewers confirm convincing evidence of enhanced plasma membrane localization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with strong agreement.

Perfect agreement on patient tissue immunohistochemistry data (C6, C34, C70). OpenEval notes independent pathologist evaluation and appropriate statistical analysis, while peer reviewers describe the correlation with high-grade DCIS as convincing. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support calcium assay data showing differential TRPV4 responses (C4, C35-C39). OpenEval emphasizes time-course measurements and priming hypothesis, while peer reviewers detail the decrease in calcium under crowding and acute influx with TRPV4 activator. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address pharmacological manipulation of TRPV4 (C40-C41 in OpenEval; C7-C8, C40, C43-C44, C46-C47 in peer review). OpenEval focuses on opposite effects of inhibition versus activation on localization, while peer reviewers emphasize multiple strategies showing good correlation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support shRNA knockdown experiments (C9, C42, C92-C96 in OpenEval; C9, C42, C92, C94, C105 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes loss-of-function evidence for TRPV4's critical role, while peer reviewers confirm genetic manipulation as part of comprehensive approach. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on TRPV4 activity and cell volume relationship. OpenEval focuses on pharmacological manipulation and correlation analysis (C43-C45, C97-C100), while peer reviewers address broader pharmacological strategies (C7-C8, C40, C43-C44, C46-C47). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support correlations between TRPV4 localization, volume, and invasiveness (C46-C49, C101-C102 in OpenEval; C45, C48-C49, C51-C53 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes high R² values and dose-response relationships, while peer reviewers confirm strong correlations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on single-cell tracking and correlations. OpenEval addresses volume-motility-invasiveness relationships with cytoskeletal changes (C50-C53, C103-C106), while peer reviewers focus on correlation analyses (C45, C48-C49, C51-C53). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on cell line selectivity testing (C54-C58, C107-C114 in OpenEval; C54-C58, C107-C110 in peer review). OpenEval systematically distinguishes mechanotransducing from non-mechanotransducing cells, while peer reviewers emphasize pathway selectivity for highly malignant invasive cell lines. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support viability controls (C73-C74). OpenEval emphasizes propidium iodide staining showing minimal cell death, while peer reviewers accept these as part of well-executed experimental design without explicit discussion. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support multiple ion channel participation (C80-C82, C91 in OpenEval; C82, C91 in peer review). OpenEval notes TRPV4 shows most dramatic relocation with coordinated response, while peer reviewers accept multi-channel findings as part of comprehensive study. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.
OpenEval supports biphasic calcium response to osmotic stress (C90) providing mechanistic insight. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Divergent evaluations on clinical applications (C10, C117, C124). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative requiring prospective validation despite supporting patient data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting biomarker potential and therapeutic targeting based on patient tissue data, though acknowledging some speculation.

Both support functional priming of relocated TRPV4 channels (C5). OpenEval cites differential calcium responses in ND versus Con cells (C39), while peer reviewers describe acute calcium influx with activator attesting to high PM channel numbers. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.
OpenEval supports synthesis showing mechanotransduction selectivity to high-grade DCIS cells (C115-C116). No direct corresponding peer review evaluation, though selectivity is addressed in peer R12.

Both support complexity of mechanotransduction pathway involving multiple ion channels (C118-C120). OpenEval notes TRPV4 as dominant player with reasonable but not directly tested coordinated action inference, while peer reviewers accept multi-channel interpretation as part of comprehensive study. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on multiple mechanical stimuli producing consistent effects (C7-C8, C121-C122 in OpenEval; C7-C8, C40, C43-C44, C46-C47 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes unified mechanotransduction mechanism across stimuli, while peer reviewers note multiple strategies showing good correlation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support background context claims (C1, C11-C13). OpenEval notes appropriate citations establishing rationale, while peer reviewers affirm the knowledge gap being addressed without questioning background. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both support clinical and experimental context (C14-C17, C68-C69 in OpenEval; C14-C17 in peer review). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations justifying model system, while peer reviewers accept background without concerns. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic background claims (C59-C61, C64-C67, C77-C78). OpenEval notes citations establishing theoretical framework, while peer reviewers accept established scientific knowledge without question. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval supports ATP2B4 plasma membrane association in MCF10CA1a cells (C79) as part of broader mechanosensitive ion transporter relocation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval rates speculative impact statement (C123) as UNCERTAIN, noting subjective claims about far-reaching implications cannot be evaluated from current data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer reviewers support reversibility findings (C71, C86-C88) as part of elegantly designed study without explicit discussion. OpenEval addresses reversibility within R1 (C71-C72) and R5 (C86-C89) but not as separate evaluation.

Peer reviewers support cytoskeletal changes and motility findings (C103-C104, C106) as part of comprehensive mechanotransduction response. OpenEval addresses these within R12 as mechanistic link to increased motility but not as separate evaluation.
